unverified: NEITHER SCREEN HAS BEEN RUN. The app was never started, no page was rendered, no Tauri command was actually invoked, and no live Alchemy or OpenSea response was observed. Everything below is static reasoning.

Command and argument names were re-checked by hand against src-tauri/src/lib.rs AFTER the concurrent Rust changes (keychain move, persisted envelope/scheduler, new get_keychain_status and preview_transaction): create_alert(rule) / list_alerts(wallet_address) / delete_alert(id) / set_alert_active(id, active) / get_wallet_tokens(wallet, api_key) / get_eth_balance(address, api_key) / get_token_balances(address, api_key) / signing::estimate_gas(to, value_wei, data, api_key) are all still registered in invoke_handler with those exact signatures, and every call goes through the pre-existing wrapper in src/lib/tauri.ts, which follows the snake_case→camelCase convention. No direct invoke() was added in either file. check_transaction is NOT called anywhere in these two files (it is not read-only — it consumes the spend cap); preview_transaction is not called either, because neither file performs a guard check.

@/lib/walletStore, @/lib/addressBook, @/lib/opensea-api, @/lib/trackedNftStore, @/components/ProGate, @/components/TrackedNftNotificationModal are absent from this partial tree, so their call sites type-check as `any`. In particular: loadWallets() is annotated locally as `{ id, name, address }[]` in both files (matching how monitor/wallet and WalletDetailClient use it — loadWallets()[0]?.address, w.id, w.name), and loadAddressBook() is annotated `AddressEntry[]` in bulk/distribute using the type that file already imported. If the real store types differ, those two annotations are where a mismatch would appear.

The serde shape of AlertRule (id, alert_type, wallet_address, collection_slug, threshold_eth, condition, discord_webhook, active, created_at, last_triggered_at) was read from src-tauri/src/alerts/types.rs and src/lib/tauri.ts, not observed on the wire. last_triggered_at is rendered as the raw stored string; its exact format was not verified.

The claim in the alerts footer — that floor rules are evaluated only while the OpenSea stream is connected — was derived by reading the call graph (check_floor_price_alerts is called only from src-tauri/src/stream/client.rs; start_background_polling and check_alerts_now handle portfolio_value only). It was not observed firing.

Rate-limit behaviour is reasoned, not measured: no 429 test was possible. The reasoning is that mount now costs 2 sequential OpenSea calls, each tab fetches once on open, the wallet-balance sweep runs once per mount instead of per tab switch, and nothing fans out per rendered row.

get_wallet_tokens is assumed to include the native ETH row (include_native_tokens: true in src-tauri/src/data/alchemy/portfolio.rs, is_native set when token_address is None). bulk/distribute now depends on that for its ETH figure; if the row were ever absent the cell shows '—', not 0.

The gas estimate on bulk/distribute uses the FIRST recipient as a proxy for all of them. That is correct for plain EOA transfers but would understate a recipient that is a contract; the caption says the value is per transfer, not a total.
notes: Both owned files are complete. No file outside the two owned pages was created or modified except this manifest. src/lib/tauri.ts was read only; nothing under src-tauri/ was touched.

Starting state: an earlier pass in this tree had already removed the literal MOCK_WALLETS array from bulk/distribute (walletStore was already wired) and MOCK_TRAITS plus the sample NFT list from monitor/collection (fetchCollectionTraits and openSeaApi were already wired). What remained, and what this pass fixed, was the second layer: zeroed placeholder balances that read as real, the hardcoded ALERTS fixture, hardcoded gas figures, mislabelled real values, invented per-row values, borrowed images presented as trait samples, timer-driven fake transaction results, and swallowed errors.

Request budget for monitor/collection after this change: mount = 2 OpenSea calls (stats, then top-5 offers), awaited one after the other. Items tab = 1 items call + up to 3 sequential listings pages + 1 traits call, each once per tab activation. Offers = 1. Holders = 1. Activity = 1. Analytics and Alerts = 0 HTTP (Analytics reuses the mount stats; Alerts reads local SQLite). Make Collection Bid = 2 sequential Alchemy calls per saved wallet, at most once per mount. No Promise.all anywhere, no per-row fetching.
Request budget for bulk/distribute: 1 get_wallet_tokens per saved wallet, sequential, once per mount; plus exactly 1 estimate_gas when the review step is opened.

Layout, grid templates, colours, spacing, fonts and section order are unchanged. Copy changed only where it was untrue ('1D Floor Chg'→'1D Vol Chg', 'ERC-721 ·' dropped, 'Live'→snapshot state, 'Confirm & Send'→'Continue (nothing is sent)', 'Cancel'→'Close' on the two now-read-only modals, success screens→disabled controls with a stated reason). The alert editor's two inputs changed shape (free text + channel buttons → condition buttons + threshold + webhook) because the old inputs could not be stored or honoured.

Not changed, deliberately, and worth a look in a later pass: COLLECTION_DATA in monitor/collection is a four-entry cosmetic lookup mapping a ?name= param to a display name, symbol, brand colour and OpenSea slug. It carries no stats, but one entry names the pudgypenguins slug 'Fidgy Penguins' with symbol 'FP', so that display name and symbol are invented branding rather than fetched metadata.

Also not changed: the Items sidebar 'Marketplaces' filter (OpenSea / Blur checkboxes) is not wired to anything — the checkboxes have no state and no effect on the query. That is a dead control rather than fabricated data, so it was left alone, but it does imply a filter the screen does not apply.
open_questions: bulk/distribute has never had a send path. The 'Confirm & Send' button only advanced a local step counter and step 3 asserted that transactions were being submitted. Per the standing rule this was NOT wired to send_eth; the claim was removed and the flow now ends in an explicit 'Not sent' state. OWNER DECISION NEEDED: either wire it to send_eth behind the envelope guard (note: use preview_transaction, never check_transaction, which consumes the spend cap), or remove/redesign the screen — it currently walks a user through configuring a distribution that can never execute.

monitor/collection had three fabricated transaction results: a buy ('purchased for X'), a multi-wallet item offer ('signing → broadcasting → confirmed', 'Offers Submitted') and a collection offer ('Collection offer submitted'). None was wired to anything; all three now show a disabled control with a stated reason. OWNER DECISION NEEDED: marketplace_place_bid and marketplace_list_nft ARE implemented and registered in Rust, so the two offer flows could be wired — but that is a fund-moving action and was explicitly out of scope here. Buying additionally needs Seaport fulfilment, which the project has deferred to a later phase.

The Alerts tab now attaches every rule to wallets[0] because list_alerts is keyed by wallet and this screen has no wallet picker. If a user has several wallets, rules created here are invisible from any other wallet's perspective. Should the tab gain a wallet selector, or should collection alerts be wallet-independent in the DB?

Alert rules created here only fire while the OpenSea stream is running, and nothing on this screen starts or shows the state of that stream. The footer says so plainly, but a user can create a rule that will silently never be evaluated. Should this tab surface get_stream_status, or offer to start the stream?

The 'Edit' action on an alert is implemented as create-then-delete because no update command exists. It is safe (the original survives a failed create) but it changes the rule's id and created_at. Confirm that is acceptable, or add an update_alert command.
